newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil to spud well at Irish Connemara oilfield.
newsitem.headline: Statoil to spud well at Irish Connemara oilfield.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday it would begin spudding this week the first well on the Connemara field west of Ireland.
The well will take about 60 days to drill and complete. It will then be put through another 60 days of test production while the JW McLean rig drills a second well for 15 days of testing.
The rig is owned by Reading & Bates Corp of the United States.
Statoil's Status Weekly newsletter said the results of the tests would determine whether Connemara will be the first oil development off Ireland's west coast.

A processing unit has been installed on the JW McLean. Oil produced during the testing will be transported to the Berge Hugin multipurpose shuttle tanker one kilometre away. The vessel is 50/50 owned by Statoil and Norwegian shipowners Bergesen ASA.
Located in 365 metres of water, Connemara was discovered in 1979 by a British Petroleum led consortium but was not considered commercial at the time, Statoil said.
